statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail remains elevated because the overnight Nasdaq discount is paired with fresh Asian technology weakness, oil above $107 and near-5% U.S. yields; fresh granular NQ retracement evidence remains unavailable.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: orange. Classification remains contingent on whether European price discovery repairs the gap with two-way rotations or shows repeated extension with shallow retracements.
headline: Elevated Tail persists before Europe open as technology, oil and rates remain aligned
body: Fresh Reuters reporting shows sharp AI-linked weakness across Asia and Brent above $107, while rates remain restrictive. The latest specific Nasdaq futures report still showed a roughly 1.1% decline versus about 0.4% for S&P futures, but current granular NQ pullback structure is not sufficiently verified.

lookbackSummary: Tail held at 19% through 21:00 UTC on September 13, rose to 24% at the Globex reopening hour, then remained 25-28% elevated through 04:00 UTC as Nasdaq futures weakness aligned with oil, rates and Asian technology stress.
outlookSummary: Tail remains elevated into Europe because technology, energy and rates signals are aligned, but direct evidence of persistent failed NQ retracements is incomplete. Risk eases conditionally with two-way European trade, then rises around the U.S. cash open and power hour only if one-way structure reappears.

forecast.analysis: The second cash-session hour stays elevated conditionally if repeated extension continues after attempted rebounds. If the opening impulse loses efficiency and rotations broaden, the forecast path shifts lower.

Late U.S. morning Tail remains elevated only if the market continues to deny meaningful retracements. Stabilizing yields, softer oil pressure, or deeper index pullbacks would weaken the one-way-path case.

Around U.S. midday, the baseline moves to WATCH if earlier directional pressure has transitioned into two-way rotations. Holding near session extremes with failed bounces would instead preserve elevated Tail.

Early U.S. afternoon risk remains in WATCH conditionally if liquidity becomes more rotational. A renewed technology-led leg with index futures holding near extremes would push Tail back into the elevated band.
The U.S. power-hour checkpoint carries elevated conditional Tail if the session remains one-way and near its extremes. A mature range with meaningful counter-moves would keep risk closer to WATCH.

At the U.S. cash-close transition, Tail remains minimally elevated if late-session directional pressure survives the closing auction. A balanced close after broad retracement would support faster de-escalation.

After the cash close, WATCH becomes the conditional baseline if the session has stopped extending and cross-asset stress is not producing a fresh equity leg. New geopolitical escalation would invalidate that easing.

Later evening risk remains WATCH if futures trade is orderly and prior extremes are not being extended. A renewed one-way move with rising oil or yields would raise Tail back above the elevated threshold.

The forecast returns to low Tail only if the evening structure shows meaningful mean reversion and no fresh directional catalyst. Extreme Stress can persist without implying a pathological price path.

Into the new UTC day, low Tail is conditional on orderly futures trade and repaired directional imbalance. Any fresh energy, rates, or technology shock would require reassessment rather than being assumed away.
Early overnight Tail stays low conditionally if two-way trading persists and prior session extremes are no longer attracting extension. Persistent extreme holding would invalidate the low-Tail path.
During early Asia, the low-Tail path depends on continued retracement capacity and stable cross-assets. Renewed technology weakness paired with higher oil or yields would raise conditional risk.

As Asian liquidity develops, Tail remains low only if directional efficiency stays limited and counter-moves remain meaningful. Fresh synchronized weakness across technology and rates would challenge that assumption.
Approaching the next Asia-to-Europe handoff, low Tail remains conditional on an orderly overnight range. A renewed unrepaired gap or repeated failed retracements would require a higher assessment.
